Quickly glancing at the repro, if you don't have the devices in the IR you should use `#hal.device.promise`.

Your issue is likely using explicit affinities but not having a topology defined. If you're trying to write your own IR as input you should use `flow.tensor.transfer` ops and not put `stream.affinity` on them _unless_ you're willing to alpha test the nascent heterogeneous support. See compiler/src/iree/compiler/Dialect/Stream/Transforms/test/elide_async_transfers.mlir for how to set up a topology.

```MLIR
    %29 = flow.tensor.update %25, %28[%c64, %c0] : tensor<64x64xf32> -> %28 as tensor<128x128xf32>

```


This still produces the same error:

```
wave.mlir:283:11: error: op affinity #hal.device.affinity<@__device_1> is not compatible with the partition affinity #hal.device.affinity<@__device_0>
    %11 = flow.tensor.transfer %10 : tensor<64x64xf16> to #hal.device.promise<@__device_1>
          ^
wave.mlir:264:3: note: called from
  func.func @isolated_benchmark(%arg0: tensor<128x64xf16>, %arg1: tensor<128x64xf16>, %arg2: tensor<128x128xf32>) -> tensor<128x128xf32> {
  ^
wave.mlir:283:11: note: see current operation: %25 = "stream.async.transfer"(%23, %7, %7) <{result_affinity = #hal.device.affinity<@__device_1>, source_affinity = #hal.device.affinity<@__device_0>}> : (!stream.resource<external>, index, index) -> !stream.resource<transient>
    %11 = flow.tensor.transfer %10 : tensor<64x64xf16> to #hal.device.promise<@__device_1>
          ^
```
### Context

We split M X K matrix into M0xK and M1xK, and likewise split matrix B along the N dimension. We then just distribute these sub-matrices to difference devices.

```
M x K -> M0xK, M1xK
N x K -> N0xK, N1xK

Device0: M0xK & N0xK
Device1: M1xK & N0xK
Device2: M0xK & N1xK
Device3: M1xK & N1xK
```

This requires broadcasting `N0xK` to both `Device0` and `Device1`, and `N1xK` to both `Device2` and `Device3`. Even with separate slice operations, IREE seems to recognize they're the same slice  and deduplicates the slices based on their source ranges, which makes sense for optimization but prevents this broadcast pattern.

### Strangeness

When playing around with this setup, when I disable Device 3 by manually updating the returns in MLIR to return independent outputs from the GEMM, it passes when I return three outputs from Device 0, 1, and 2.

```
M x K -> M0xK, M1xK
N x K -> N0xK, N1xK

Device0: M0xK & N0xK
Device1: M1xK & N0xK
Device2: M0xK & N1xK
// Device3: M1xK & N1xK --> we remove this.
```

The reason why that is strange is because technically we are still broadcasting N0xK, and M0xK.

### Question

Is there a way to force IREE to treat these as independent transfers, or is there a different pattern I should use for this kind of multi-device broadcast?

[updated_fail.mlir.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21782940/updated_fail.mlir.txt)
[updated_pass.mlir.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21782939/updated_pass.mlir.txt)

Passing example:
`iree-compile updated_pass.mlir.txt --iree-hip-target=gfx942 --iree-hal-target-device=hip[0] --iree-hal-target-device=hip[1] --iree-hal-target-device=hip[2] --iree-hal-target-device=hip[3] --iree-opt-level=O3`

Failing example:
`iree-compile updated_fail.mlir.txt --iree-hip-target=gfx942 --iree-hal-target-device=hip[0] --iree-hal-target-device=hip[1] --iree-hal-target-device=hip[2] --iree-hal-target-device=hip[3] --iree-opt-level=O3`

issue.body:
### What happened?

I have a distributed gemm.mlir generated through Wave DSL. I am using flow dialect to orchestrate splitting and dispatching inputs to a number of GPUs. I am noticing that when the GEMM is distributed to more than three devices the compile exits with an error:
```

(.venv) $ iree-compile /home/sanketp/issue/pass.mlir --iree-hip-target=gfx942 --iree-hal-target-device=hip[0] --iree-hal-target-device=hip[1] --iree-hal-target-device=hip[2] --iree-opt-level=O3 -o=gemm_example/gemm.vmfb
(.venv) $ iree-compile /home/sanketp/issue/fail.mlir --iree-hip-target=gfx942 --iree-hal-target-device=hip[0] --iree-hal-target-device=hip[1] --iree-hal-target-device=hip[2] --iree-hal-target-device=hip[3] --iree-opt-level=O3 -o=gemm_example/gemm.vmfb
/home/sanketp/issue/fail.mlir:280:11: error: op affinity #hal.device.affinity<@__device_1> is not compatible with the partition affinity #hal.device.affinity<@__device_0>
    %13 = flow.dispatch @gemm::@gemm(%1, %5, %9) {stream.affinity = #hal.device.affinity<@__device_1>} : (tensor<64x64xf16>, tensor<64x64xf16>, tensor<64x64xf32>) -> %9
          ^
/home/sanketp/issue/fail.mlir:264:3: note: called from
  func.func @isolated_benchmark(%arg0: tensor<128x64xf16>, %arg1: tensor<128x64xf16>, %arg2: tensor<128x128xf32>) -> (tensor<64x64xf32>, tensor<64x64xf32>, tensor<64x64xf32>, tensor<64x64xf32>) {
  ^
/home/sanketp/issue/fail.mlir:280:11: note: see current operation: %28 = "stream.async.transfer"(%20, %7, %7) <{result_affinity = #hal.device.affinity<@__device_1>, source_affinity = #hal.device.affinity<@__device_0>}> : (!stream.resource<external>, index, index) -> !stream.resource<transient>
    %13 = flow.dispatch @gemm::@gemm(%1, %5, %9) {stream.affinity = #hal.device.affinity<@__device_1>} : (tensor<64x64xf16>, tensor<64x64xf16>, tensor<64x64xf32>) -> %9
          ^
```

**What I expected:**
The compilation should succeed when distributing the GEMM operation across 4 devices, similar to how it works with 3 devices. The transfers between devices appear to be correctly specified with matching affinities.

### Steps to reproduce your issue

[fail.mlir.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21726039/fail.mlir.txt)
[pass.mlir.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21726040/pass.mlir.txt)

To reproduce the passing case:
`iree-compile /home/sanketp/issue/pass.mlir --iree-hip-target=gfx942 --iree-hal-target-device=hip[0] --iree-hal-target-device=hip[1] --iree-hal-target-device=hip[2] --iree-opt-level=O3 -o=gemm_example/gemm.vmfb`

To reproduce the failing case:
`iree-compile /home/sanketp/issue/fail.mlir --iree-hip-target=gfx942 --iree-hal-target-device=hip[0] --iree-hal-target-device=hip[1] --iree-hal-target-device=hip[2] --iree-hal-target-device=hip[3] --iree-opt-level=O3 -o=gemm_example/gemm.vmfb`

### What component(s) does this issue relate to?

Compiler

### Version information


The compiler version I am using is :
```
(.venv) $ iree-compile --version
IREE (https://iree.dev):
  IREE compiler version 3.7.0rc20250724 @ 530d3552e75010726d63f768a476b79e0868914b
  LLVM version 22.0.0git
  Optimized build
```

### Additional context

Compilation fails on `ScheduleExecutionPass` with the message that partition affinity does not match the dispatch affinity (see error in What happened? section). However, the mlir in question seems correct at a glance:

```
  %12 = stream.async.transfer %4 : !stream.resource<external>{%c8192} from(#hal.device.affinity<@__device_0>) -> to(#hal.device.affinity<@__device_1>) !stream.resource<transient>{%c8192}
  %13 = stream.async.transfer %5 : !stream.resource<external>{%c8192} from(#hal.device.affinity<@__device_0>) -> to(#hal.device.affinity<@__device_1>) !stream.resource<transient>{%c8192}
  %14 = stream.async.transfer %8 : !stream.resource<external>{%c16384} from(#hal.device.affinity<@__device_0>) -> to(#hal.device.affinity<@__device_1>) !stream.resource<external>{%c16384}
  %15 = stream.async.dispatch on(#hal.device.affinity<@__device_1>) @gemm::@gemm(%12[%c0 to %c8192 for %c8192], %13[%c0 to %c8192 for %c8192], %14[%c0 to %c16384 for %c16384]) : (!stream.resource<transient>{%c8192}, !stream.resource<transient>{%c8192}, !stream.resource<external>{%c16384}) -> %14{%c16384}
```

We create slices on device_0 and transfer them to device_1 before calling gemm on them.
